A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original reward-modeling and preference-alignment experiments, including accuracy, deception scores, sensitivity analyses, and mitigation experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds larger-model evaluations, expanded DPO results, and an empirical case study.

M1.justification: The weak-supervision procedure, explicit and implicit conflict objectives, confidence filtering, and bootstrapping method are retained. The loss equations added to the main text already appear in v1 Appendix B. LoRA is introduced as a supplemental experimental configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions use CAI-Harmless and HH-RLHF helpfulness data for reward modeling and preference alignment under the same conflict scenarios. The additional models and illustrative sample do not introduce a new dataset, task, or input environment.

E2.justification: The ground-truth-trained ceilings, no-conflict references, SimPO/DPO methods, and filtering/bootstrapping comparisons are retained. V2 extends model configurations without adding a distinct comparison method.

E3.justification: V2 extends DPO evaluation to OPT-6.7B and Mistral-7B and introduces LLaMA-3-8B/70B and LLaMA-3.1-8B experiments. Appendix G uses matched LoRA configurations and a learning rate of 3 × 10^-4 for the added LLaMA models. Existing data splits, metrics, and original training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a same-size LLaMA-3 versus LLaMA-3.1 comparison examining capability versus parameter count, and Appendix K adds a concrete deception case study. Existing conflict-strength, confidence-threshold, filtering, and bootstrapping analyses remain. The new Figure 8 largely redisplays the earlier knowledge-area versus deception-score comparison.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix C.1 and v2 Appendix D.1 both explicitly report one run per experiment because of computational cost. Neither version adds repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial DPO and LLaMA results in Figures 12–14 and sample-level probabilities in Table 1. Existing knowledge-area proportions change from 0.13/0.15/0.19 in v1 Figure 6(b–d) to 0.14/0.17/0.22 in v2 Figure 7(b–d), while their deception scores remain 0.12/0.34/0.56. These are added results and numerical revisions, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The knowledge-space definitions, deception-score formula, and alignment objectives remain mathematically equivalent. V2 repeats existing appendix equations in the main text and changes notation, without adding a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the existence of conflict-associated weak-to-strong deception, its relationship to capability gaps, and partial mitigation through bootstrapping. V2 expands supporting evidence and emphasizes these findings; v1 already states them in its results and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations distinguishing capability from parameter count and hypotheses about sample-distribution cues and intermediate-model knowledge. It explicitly leaves helpfulness supervision from the same weak teacher to future work. The earlier 7B-size limitation is removed following the larger-model experiments.

D1.justification: V2 adds eight NVIDIA A800 GPUs to the reported hardware and specifies LoRA placement in attention/FFN modules, rank 8, alpha 16, and the additional learning rate. It also clarifies that filtering confidence concerns the correct label. Existing training details and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Denison et al. on reward tampering, Guo et al. on controllable preference optimization, Zhou et al. on weak-to-strong search, and LLaMA 3.1, while removing the GLUE citation. The central positioning remains unchanged. Burns et al.'s publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and selected explanatory passages, expands the author list, includes existing objective equations in the main text, folds conflict-strength discussion into Section 5.3, and moves limitations to Appendix A. Most of the original narrative and procedural text remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure resizing and relocation. V2 adds the conceptual Figure 2, comparison Figure 8, LLaMA Figure 14, and case-study Table 1, and restructures the original DPO figure into Figures 12–13. Figure 7(b) introduces an axis/caption model-name mismatch.

improvement.justification: The expanded DPO and larger-model experiments address coverage gaps explicitly acknowledged in v1, while the added implementation details and case study improve assessability. The gains remain limited by unchanged single-run evidence and new labeling errors: Figure 7(b) disagrees on the model identity, and Table 1 labels confidence 0.99 as Strong-Unknown despite Appendix K describing Strong-Known. Overall, the additional support provides a modest net improvement.
